title: worldfilm Shot Spec — shotspec-film 0.1 plus world, camera, reference, blur, footage and audibility
description: A worldfilm spec is a valid shotspec-film Shot Spec (every shotspec gate still applies) plus the optional blocks below. Old ShotSpecs validate unchanged; blocks are optional at the schema level and used by the stage that needs them.

camera.description: Camera dial, set once per film at intake (a branding decision). 1 Locked, 2 Anchored, 3 Motivated, 4 Flowing, 5 Perpetual. The dial governs the camera only; elements may keep moving at every setting. A per-shot shots[].camera.dial overrides it for that shot.

signature_moves.description: named moves this film is allowed to repeat (e.g. push, orbit, crane, dolly, rack); other moves should vary scene to scene

max_hold_s.description: longest the camera may rest motionless where the effective dial is 4-5 (a project choice; 0.5 s is a common starting point)

log_space.description: zoom / distance keyed in log space so a 2x push reads the same at any scale

rest_drift.description: Optional micro-drift for camera rests in shots whose effective dial (shots[].camera.dial, else project.camera.dial) is at least min_dial. Locked or anchored shots below min_dial do not drift. Recommended shape: an ellipse, height in quadrature with the lateral sway at one angular rate, so the drift velocity never passes through zero (a one-axis sine stops at every turning point, every pi/omega seconds, which a frozen-time gate reads as frozen). Offset added to the rest pose: lateral = A(t) * (lateral_units * sin(omega_rad_s * t) + slow_lateral_units * sin(slow_omega_rad_s * t + 1)), vertical = Av(t) * vertical_units * cos(omega_rad_s * t), where A(t) = 1 + the sine-windowed boost factors active at t and Av(t) is the same sum without boosts whose axes are 'lateral'. All parameters are in world units and must be scaled to the scene: a starting point is lateral_units of roughly 0.2-1 % of the camera-to-subject distance, vertical_units 0.5-1x lateral, and omega_rad_s giving a period of a few seconds; tune by eye and by the frozen-time margin. Use shape 'none' (or omit the block) when rests should stay still.

shape.description: 'ellipse' applies the quadrature drift above; 'none' disables rest drift

lateral_units.description: half-width of the lateral sway in world units (scale to the scene)

vertical_units.description: half-height in world units, in quadrature with the lateral sway; 0 makes a one-axis sway that stops at its turning points

omega_rad_s.description: angular rate of the ellipse in rad/s (period = 2*pi/omega)

slow_lateral_units.description: optional slower lateral component in world units, so the path does not repeat exactly

slow_omega_rad_s.description: angular rate of the slow lateral component in rad/s

axes.description: 'lateral' leaves the height alone so a framing target can settle in one direction during the window

boosts.description: optional windows where the drift is amplified (a designed rest); each window lies inside the film

min_dial.description: rest drift applies only to shots whose effective dial is at least this value

reference.description: Measured reference block from measure_reference.py (numbers only, never copied pixels): what the styleframes are matched against, and a basis for choosing per-project gate limits.

compare_sheet.description: path of the approved compare_frames.mjs sheet

approved.description: the human approved the styleframes against this block before any motion was built

blur.description: Sub-frame motion blur for the master. route 'playwright' uses capture_subframes.mjs; 'engine' is reserved for a renderer that exposes motion blur; 'none' delivers the sharp render. Drafts render without it.

world.description: The simulated world the shots film: state precomputed once at load, a pure render(t), anchors(t) for labels and events(t) for sound.

data_files.description: data files the world reads; every value on screen must trace to facts_file

precompute_note.description: what is simulated once at load so render(t) stays pure

options.description: optional extra createWorld(canvas, {width, height, ...options}) options for the primary composition; keys are defined by the project's world module

footage.description: Real footage entering as a separated subject layer (sam_separate.py).

variants.description: Optional extra aspects or sizes. Each delivered variant is its own film at the gates: its own composition, world options and label hold line, its own render, its own pops / luma / run_gates reports (gates/master-<slug>-<id>-<WxH>/) and its own PROGRESS.md row; it never inherits the primary size's pass. Adding a variant option must leave the primary render unchanged (frame_hash on a primary draft proves it). build.sh renders a variant when deliver is true or when its id is named in the VARIANTS environment variable.

id.description: short slug used in file names, e.g. vertical or square

composition.description: composition HTML for this variant, relative to the project root

world_options.description: optional createWorld options only this variant turns on; keys are defined by the project's world module

label_hold_frac.description: hold line for anchored labels in this variant (fraction of frame height)

fov_scale.description: optional tan(fov/2) multiplier applied to the pose graph's fov in this aspect; choose it from the variant's framing

gates.description: always 'own': the variant's render is gated on its own

deliver.description: build.sh renders, muxes and gates this variant in a full build

gates.description: How the gates are run and read (run_gates.py via npx hyperframes, check_gate_report.py, detect_pops.py, luma_floor.py, loop_seam.py, frame_hash.py). A skipped gate is not a passed gate. frozen_time is sampled at 10 fps, and a blurred or containerised master can read one sample differently from a draft, so a draft passes only with frozen_margin_samples of margin. Limits may be chosen per project from the measured reference; script defaults apply when a field is omitted.

allow_skip.description: gates this spec legitimately cannot feed (e.g. handoff without a carry object, swatch without swatch points); record the reason in GAUNTLET.jsonl

hyperframes_cmd.description: the gate runner command; always 'npx hyperframes' (run_gates.py splits it on spaces, so a path is not allowed)

cta_tail_s.description: final seconds excluded from frozen_time as an end card (run_gates default 1.5)

hard_cuts_s.description: intended hard-cut times; detect_pops reports them and the blur shutter never crosses them

pops_allow_s.description: intended one-frame events (e.g. a designed flash) detect_pops should accept

luma_min.description: per-window mean-luma floor for luma_floor.py (library default 35); set from the measured reference for intentionally dark films

luma_tail_s.description: seconds at the end that luma_floor.py ignores (e.g. a fade to black)

require.description: gates that must be present in every gate report (check_gate_report.py --require)

loop_seam.description: the film is a loop: run loop_seam.py on every delivered master

frame_hash_ab.description: full builds render the primary picture twice in Docker and compare decoded frame hashes

delivery.description: What a full build delivers beyond the primary master (project.sizes[0] at project.fps). Fields left unset are skipped and reported.

poster_t.description: time of the poster frame; omit for no poster

srt.description: write captions as SRT from shots[].text (tools/srt.py)

camera.description: Pose graph for this shot. Distance and zoom are keyed in log space when project.camera.log_space is true, interpolated with a monotone cubic (no overshoot) unless a pose names an ease; velocity peaks are where blur and whoosh-like cues belong.

move.description: named move (e.g. push, pull, orbit, crane, dolly, pan, rack, hold)

velocity_peak_s.description: time of the fastest camera motion in the shot (where blur and a motion cue belong)

settle_s.description: when the move has settled (reading holds start here)

dial.description: optional per-shot exception to project.camera.dial (e.g. a locked insert in a flowing film). Name the exception and its reason in MOTION.md. Rest drift follows the effective dial.

framing_target.description: A shot whose camera is solved from where something must sit on screen instead of keyed by hand: name the world point, key its screen position densely (<= key_step_s apart), derive the pose from it, and assert the projected quantity in tools/sweep.mjs (settles in one direction, then holds within slack).

point.description: anchor name returned by anchors(t), or 'x,y,z' in world units

key_step_s.description: the pose is keyed at least this densely while the target is active

assert.description: what the sweep asserts about the projected quantity in [t_in, hold_from_s]

hold_from_s.description: from here the projected quantity must hold (within hold_slack_px per frame)

slack_px.description: reversal allowed per frame while settling

hold_slack_px.description: movement allowed per frame during the hold

world_anchors.description: Labels projected from world anchors: the text follows a world point and is set at a fixed screen size. Placement rule (film/place_label.js, shared by the HUD and the sweep): the plate sits above its anchor; when that overlaps the object it names and the world provides side candidates, it moves beside the object (<a>-right, then <a>-left; <a>-right-outer / <a>-left-outer give the outer edge to clear). Side candidates are optional: anchors(cam) returns them only for objects that need them. Then the plate is clamped to the safe area, kept out of any reserved readout box and the caption zone, held at hold_line_frac, and pushed up deterministically on collision. No plate may touch the object it names in any frame it is up (sweep_lib labelsClear).

text_id.description: the shots[].text entry this label shows

placement.description: 'auto' is above, then beside-right, then beside-left when side candidates exist

hold_line_frac.description: the plate stops following its anchor below this fraction of the frame height and holds, so it never races a passing object out of frame (place_label.js default 0.76)

footage_layer.description: Where the separated subject sits in this shot's depth stack.

frame_offset.description: footage frame shown at the shot's t_in

audio.description: Optional audio contract. Synthesized audio: set cue_sheet (audio/make_cues.py writes it, synth_sfx.py renders it, prove_audible.py checks each cue). A supplied track: project.music.src. Picture only: neither.

cue_sheet.description: path of the synth_sfx.py cue sheet JSON

audibility_db.description: required in-band lift over the bed at the cue's peak (prove_audible default 4)

event.description: the events(t) entry this cue is locked to

silence.description: optional exact digital-silence windows [[from_s, to_s], ...]: zeros in every output, carved by synth_sfx.py and proven by prove_audible.py --silence. build.sh reads them from here.

music_only.description: Optional music-only export: the score stem mastered on its own with synth_sfx.py --master-stem (a stem carries the mix's gain and alone reads under the loudness target). build.sh produces it only when this block names a stem; record the result here.
